wa_columbia_gorge.blurb: Most climbers who come to this Washington stretch of the Columbia River live closer to Portland than to any Washington city. Basalt is the rock. Beacon Rock, a huge volcanic plug rising straight from the river, is the multi-pitch trad destination, while Ozone, OH8 and Farside / Dropzone hold single-pitch sport and trad lines. Bouldering is a large part of the mix, at Empire Boulders, Hamilton Boulders and several smaller groups, mostly in the easy to middle V grades. Roped climbs lean trad with a solid sport minority, centred on 5.9 to 5.11, and a thin tail of harder lines above that. Rock quality is uneven in places, but the setting is hard to beat.

nv_calico_basin.blurb: Calico Basin sits in the Red Rock area of southern Nevada, around a small residential basin. The rock is sandstone, and the climbing is a broad mix: short sport and trad routes, plus a very large number of boulders. Kraft Mountain Area, Moderate Mecca, Ash Spring and The Fringe are among its biggest sectors. Roped routes run mostly from 5.8 to 5.12, with 5.10 and 5.11 the most common, so there is plenty for intermediates and a decent number of harder pitches. Boulder problems span V0 to about V7, with a handful harder. Sandstone here is fragile and gets damaged easily when wet, so conditions matter after storms.

qc_val_david.blurb: Val-David lies in the Laurentians of Quebec, in the rugged North River valley. Its cliffs are crystalline Precambrian rock, and the routes range from short pitches to walls over 100 metres. Bouldering is the largest single draw, and the roped climbing splits between trad and sport, with a few aid and ice lines. Mont-King is mostly trad, and La Bleue, Mont-Césaire and L'Aiguille add more crags. The grade spread is wide: plenty of 5.7 to 5.9, a big middle around 5.10 to 5.12, and a few lines in the 5.13s. Boulder problems stretch from V0 well into the upper grades, with many in the middle range.

ut_san_rafael_swell.blurb: The San Rafael Swell is a large, sparsely populated uplift in central Utah, cut by an interstate and split here into a north and a south section. Climbing is on sandstone and leans heavily to trad, with some aid and a smaller amount of sport and bouldering. Buckhorn Wash is known for crack climbing on Wingate sandstone, with towers nearby, while the San Rafael Reef offers very long slab routes on mostly good rock with serious runouts. Most routes fall between 5.7 and 5.11, with the heart of it around 5.9 and 5.10. It is on the adventurous end of the spectrum, and crowds are far thinner than in Moab.

wi_central.blurb: This part of Wisconsin stretches from La Crosse and the upper Mississippi across to Eau Claire and the central sands. Bouldering makes up the biggest share, with sport and trad close behind and a bit of top-roping and ice. Petenwell, above the Wisconsin River near Necedah, is a sandstone ridge with walls over 100 feet carrying sport and trad lines. Hillbilly Hollow is a small sandstone bluff with short routes, and Grandad Bluff is a city-park bluff above the Mississippi with bolted lines on rock that can be loose. Roped climbs mostly sit between 5.7 and 5.11, and boulder problems cluster in the easy to middle grades.

ca_holcomb_valley_pinnacles.blurb: The Pinnacles sit just north of Big Bear Lake at the eastern end of Holcomb Valley, in the San Bernardino Mountains at roughly 7,500 feet. The rock is heavily featured granite, and quality runs from fair to excellent. Sport routes dominate, with trad cracks and slabs mixed in and a large bouldering collection too. The grades are friendly: most roped routes are 5.10 or easier, with a strong run of 5.10s and a small number of harder lines. The pinnacles are split into Central, North, South, West and East groups, with Central the largest. Late spring through early fall is the usual window, shaded walls help in summer, and winter depends on snowfall.
